Bornholm GC4 Factor Page

Read This Page In 30 Seconds

This page explains one factor from four angles:

  1. where it is high/low on the map,
  2. how unusual values are (z-score),
  3. how it differs by cluster (class_km),
  4. which indicators define it (loadings across k).

Rule of thumb: high score = “more of this factor pattern”, low score = “less”.

Spatial View: F5

Use layer toggles to switch between:

  • raw factor score,
  • standardized score (z-score),
  • cluster overlay.

Hotspots/coldspots are simple flags of unusually high/low values.

**Key takeaway:** `F5` has 44 hotspot hexagons and 12 coldspot hexagons using z-threshold ±1.5.

Distribution and Class Context

The histogram shows the overall spread of F5 across Bornholm.
The boxplot shows how that spread differs between clusters.

**Key takeaway:** Typical `F5` value is -0.253 (middle 50% from -0.571 to 0.313).
**Key takeaway:** Cluster 7 has the highest median `F5` (5.985).

F5 Loadings vs K (Mean)

This plot shows whether interpretation of F5 stays similar when neighborhood size changes (k = 10 ... 1000).
More stable lines = more robust factor meaning.

**Key takeaway:** Most stable contributor across k is `gc_cultural_and_historical_conservation_v_shr_034ee6`.
